On the first day of his second term, President Donald Trump signed a record-breaking series of Executive Orders (“EOs”) aimed at swiftly implementing his agenda and reversing several policies of the previous administration.
EOs are written instruments through which a president can issue directives to shape policy.

Although the U.S. Constitution does not address EOs and no statute grants the president the general power to issue them, authority to issue such orders is accepted as an inherent aspect of presidential power, though their legal effect depends on various considerations. (CRS).
It is important to note that the full impact on various industries remains uncertain.
This uncertainty stems from potential legal challenges that may arise, as well as the need for further details and clarifications on the implementation of these orders from the administration.
Consequently, while we continue to monitor developments closely, it is advisable for stakeholders to stay informed and prepared for possible changes that could affect their operations.

See below a list of the EOs and other significant actions signed by President Donald Trump so far, as well as the memorandum from the Office of Management and Budget ("OMB") pausing all federal funding.
This list will be updated weekly as more are published.
For those EOs and memorandums that have had clarifications issued, we have included the clarification in italics immediately under the related EO/memo.
The descriptions of these orders are taken from the language used in the orders themselves.
This EO establishes strict controls over federal hiring to maintain a reduced and efficient workforce aligned with the administration’s priorities.
It mandates that no civilian federal position may be filled or created unless explicitly permitted, and requires agencies to form Strategic Hiring Committees to oversee hiring decisions.

Agencies must submit Annual Staffing Plans and quarterly updates to the Office of Personnel Management (“OPM”) and the Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”), prioritizing roles in national security, immigration enforcement, and public safety.
The EO outlines exceptions for certain positions and allows OPM to grant exemptions.
It also prohibits outsourcing as a means to bypass hiring restrictions and ensures that essential services like Social Security and veterans’ benefits remain unaffected.
A joint implementation report is due within 180 days.
This EO focuses on leveraging artificial intelligence (“AI”) to combat pediatric cancer, the leading cause of disease-related death among children in the United States.

It builds upon the ongoing Childhood Cancer Data Initiative (“CCDI”) by directing the Make America Healthy Again (“MAHA”) Commission and federal agencies to accelerate AI-driven research, improve data infrastructure, and enhance clinical trial design.

The EO emphasizes expanding federal and private investment, improving data sharing and interoperability, and empowering patients and families with control over their health data, all while ensuring privacy protection and compliance with existing laws.
This EO extends the operation of 22 federal advisory committees until September 30, 2027.
These committees span various domains including national security, health, education, environment, and monument preservation, and are overseen by designated federal departments or agencies.
The EO delegates the president’s responsibilities under the Federal Advisory Committee Act to the heads of these departments and supersedes sections of a previous EO (14109).
It also clarifies that the EO does not alter existing legal authorities or budgetary functions and does not create enforceable legal rights.
This EO affirms the United States' commitment to guaranteeing the security and territorial integrity of the State of Qatar in response to foreign aggression.
It recognizes Qatar’s longstanding partnership with the United States, particularly in hosting American forces and supporting regional stability.
The EO declares that any armed attack on Qatar will be treated as a threat to U.S. peace and security, prompting diplomatic, economic, or military responses.
It directs coordinated contingency planning among U.S. defense and intelligence agencies and calls for continued diplomatic collaboration with Qatar, especially in conflict mediation.
All federal agencies are instructed to implement the EO in accordance with existing laws and budgetary constraints.
This EO determines that TikTok's proposed divestiture of its U.S. operations constitutes a “qualified divestiture” under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act.
The EO outlines a framework in which TikTok will be operated by a new U.S.-based joint venture, majority-owned by American investors, with ByteDance Ltd. holding less than 20 percent ownership.
This structure removes foreign adversary control and operational ties, including over algorithms and data storage, which will now be managed and monitored by trusted U.S. security partners.

The EO also suspends enforcement of the Act for 120 days to allow the divestiture to proceed and affirms the Attorney General’s exclusive authority to enforce the Act, precluding state or private enforcement.
It further amends prior EOs related to ByteDance’s acquisition of Musical.ly and reserves presidential authority for future actions to protect national security.
This EO designates Antifa as a domestic terrorist organization.

The EO asserts that Antifa operates as a militarist, anarchist group that seeks to overthrow the U.S. government through coordinated violence, including armed standoffs, assaults on law enforcement, and suppression of political speech.
It accuses Antifa of recruiting and radicalizing youth, concealing its operations and funding, and collaborating with other entities to advance political violence.

The EO directs federal agencies to use all applicable authorities to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle Antifa’s operations, including prosecuting those who fund or support its activities, while affirming that the EO must be implemented in accordance with existing laws.
This EO establishes the "Gold Card" visa program, aimed at realigning U.S. immigration policy to prioritize national interests.

Overseen by the Secretary of Commerce, the program offers expedited immigrant visa eligibility to foreign individuals or entities who make significant financial gifts—$1 million for individuals and $2 million for corporations—to the Department of Commerce.
These contributions are treated as evidence of exceptional business ability and national benefit, qualifying applicants under existing immigration statutes.
The funds will be used to promote American commerce and industry.

The EO mandates interagency coordination for implementation within 90 days, including application procedures, fee structures, and potential program expansion, while emphasizing compliance with existing laws and national security safeguards.

This EO establishes an Emergency Board to investigate unresolved labor disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and several unions, including the Transportation Communications Union and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen.

Acting under Section 9A of the Railway Labor Act, the Board—comprised of three impartial members appointed by the President—will begin its work on September 18, 2025, and must report its findings within 30 days.
For 120 days following its creation, no changes to the disputed conditions may occur unless agreed upon by both parties.
The Board’s records will be maintained by the National Mediation Board, and the Department of Transportation will cover publication costs.
This EO further extends the enforcement delay of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act as it applies to TikTok.

This extension, now lasting until December 16, 2025, prohibits the Department of Justice from taking any enforcement actions or imposing penalties related to noncompliance with the Act during the specified period or any time prior to the EO.
The Attorney General is directed to issue guidance and letters affirming no violations or liabilities for affected entities.
The EO also asserts the Executive’s exclusive authority over enforcement, warning against attempts by states or private parties to intervene, and mandates DOJ to defend this authority.
This EO restores the historical name “Department of War” as a secondary title for the Department of Defense, citing its legacy and symbolic strength dating back to its founding in 1789.

The EO authorizes the use of titles such as “Secretary of War” and similar designations for subordinate officials in ceremonial and non-statutory contexts, while maintaining existing statutory references to the Department of Defense.
It directs the Secretary to notify Congress of any entities adopting the new designation and to recommend legislative and executive actions within 60 days to formally rename the department.
The EO emphasizes symbolic clarity and national resolve, while ensuring compliance with existing laws and budgetary constraints.
This EO modifies the scope of reciprocal tariffs and establishes procedures for implementing trade and security agreements in response to a national emergency declared in EO 14257.

The EO updates tariff schedules and outlines conditions under which tariffs may be reduced or suspended, particularly for trading partners who enter into meaningful economic and national security agreements with the United States.

It emphasizes the importance of reciprocal trade to address persistent U.S. goods trade deficits and national security threats, and delegates authority to the Secretary of Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative to implement these changes.

The EO also introduces a list of imports eligible for zero percent tariffs under certain agreements and sets procedures for monitoring, recommending, and executing further actions based on evolving trade conditions.
This EO is aimed at intensifying U.S. efforts to protect American nationals from wrongful detention abroad.

Citing the Levinson Act, the EO empowers the Secretary of State to designate foreign governments as "State Sponsors of Wrongful Detention" based on specific criteria, such as direct involvement or support of such detentions.
Once designated, the United States may impose sanctions, travel restrictions, and limit foreign assistance and exports to the offending country.

The EO also outlines conditions for terminating such designations and clarifies definitions and legal boundaries to ensure consistent implementation without infringing on lawful U.S. activities or rights.
This EO implements the United States–Japan Agreement, establishing a new trade framework aimed at reducing the U.S. trade deficit and strengthening national security.
It introduces a baseline 15% tariff on nearly all Japanese imports, with sector-specific exceptions for aerospace, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and critical natural resources.

In return, Japan commits to significantly increasing purchases of U.S. agricultural and industrial goods and investing $550 billion in the U.S. economy, expected to create hundreds of thousands of jobs.
The order also outlines procedures for tariff adjustments, monitoring Japan’s compliance, and delegating authority to relevant federal agencies to enforce and modify trade regulations as needed.

This EO mandates a return to classical and traditional architectural styles for major federal buildings, particularly in Washington, D.C., emphasizing designs that inspire civic virtue and reflect the dignity of the American government.

It criticizes modernist and brutalist styles for being unpopular and unrecognizable as civic structures, and directs the General Services Administration (“GSA”) to prioritize classical architecture in new projects and renovations.
The order outlines specific definitions, guiding principles, and procedural requirements to ensure public buildings are visually uplifting, regionally respectful, and economically feasible.
It also establishes oversight mechanisms, including a senior advisor for architectural design and performance metrics for GSA officials, to enforce compliance with the new architectural standards.

This EO expands exclusions from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program for certain federal agencies and subdivisions whose primary functions involve intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work.
The order amends Executive Order 12171 to include units within the Bureau of Reclamation, specific subdivisions of the Department of Commerce, NASA, and the U.S. Agency for Global Media.
It also extends the deadline for orders issued under Executive Order 14251 by the Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs, allowing them to take effect within 15 days of this new order.
The EO includes standard provisions on severability and clarifies that it does not create enforceable legal rights.

This EO directs federal agencies to identify and potentially suspend or terminate funding to jurisdictions that have substantially eliminated cash bail for crimes posing a clear threat to public safety.
Citing concerns over repeat offenses and risks to law enforcement and the public, the order mandates the Attorney General to compile and maintain a list of such jurisdictions.

It emphasizes that federal resources should not support policies that allow potentially dangerous individuals to be released without bail, and calls for a reevaluation of federal support in alignment with this policy, subject to legal and budgetary constraints.
This EO addresses a declared crime emergency in Washington, D.C., citing the District’s cashless bail policies as a key contributor to public safety concerns.
It mandates federal law enforcement to detain arrestees in federal custody whenever legally possible and pursue federal charges to prevent the release of dangerous suspects.
The Attorney General is directed to review and potentially revise Metropolitan Police Department policies and assess whether D.C. continues to prohibit cash bail for serious offenses.
If such policies persist, federal agencies may take actions—including funding decisions and service provisions—to pressure the District to change its approach.
The order emphasizes adherence to applicable laws and does not create enforceable legal rights.
This EO directs federal agencies to prioritize enforcement of laws against desecration of the American Flag, particularly when such acts incite violence or violate civil or criminal statutes.
While acknowledging First Amendment protections, the order emphasizes prosecuting flag desecration that constitutes “fighting words” or incites imminent lawless action.

It instructs the Attorney General to pursue legal action and coordinate with state and local authorities when applicable and authorizes immigration-related penalties—including visa denial and deportation—for foreign nationals involved in flag desecration.
The order asserts its implementation must align with existing laws and does not create enforceable legal rights.
This EO expands measures to address the declared crime emergency in Washington, D.C.

Building on EO 14333, the order directs federal agencies to bolster law enforcement capacity by hiring additional Park Police and prosecutors, creating specialized units within the Department of Justice and the National Guard, and enhancing coordination among federal, state, and local entities.

It also mandates investigations into housing safety compliance by the Department of Housing and Urban Development, transit safety inspections by the Department of Transportation, and potential updates to D.C. police protocols.
The order emphasizes rapid deployment capabilities and interagency cooperation to restore public safety and order in the capital.
This EO establishes the “America by Design” initiative to modernize and enhance the usability and aesthetics of federal digital and physical services.

It creates a National Design Studio (“NDS”) within the White House and introduces a Chief Design Officer to lead efforts in recruiting top design talent, coordinating with agencies, and implementing innovative solutions.
Agencies are directed to prioritize improvements to high-impact websites and facilities, with initial results expected by July 4, 2026.

The initiative aims to reduce duplicative design costs, improve public trust, and ensure compliance with existing digital experience laws, all while delivering more efficient and visually appealing government services.
This EO revokes Executive Order 14036, which was originally signed on July 9, 2021, to promote competition in the American economy.
The new order clarifies that it does not alter existing legal authorities of executive departments or agencies, nor does it affect the functions of the Office of Management and Budget.
It also states that the order must be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and available appropriations, and it does not create any enforceable legal rights.
The Department of Justice will bear the publication costs of the order.
This EO aims at boosting U.S. competitiveness in the commercial space industry.
The order outlines a multi-agency effort to streamline regulations, expedite environmental reviews, and eliminate bureaucratic barriers to space launch and reentry operations.
It mandates reforms to licensing procedures, spaceport infrastructure development, and novel space activity authorizations, with specific timelines for agency actions.

The order also elevates leadership roles within the Departments of Transportation and Commerce to prioritize innovation and deregulation, reinforcing the administration’s commitment to ensuring American leadership in space exploration and commercial space activities by 2030.
This EO aims to strengthen the resilience of the American pharmaceutical supply chain by replenishing the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (“SAPIR”).

It mandates the Department of Health and Human Services, through the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (“ASPR”), to identify approximately 26 critical drugs and secure a six-month supply of their active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), prioritizing domestic sources.
The order also calls for updating the 2022 list of essential medicines, planning for a second SAPIR repository, and repurposing existing funds to support these efforts.
It criticizes the previous administration for failing to advance domestic pharmaceutical production and emphasizes national security and public health preparedness.
This EO extends the suspension of certain country-specific ad valorem duties on imports from the People’s Republic of China (“PRC”) until November 10, 2025.
This action builds on previous orders responding to persistent U.S. trade deficits and retaliatory tariffs from the PRC.
The suspension, originally enacted in May 2025, reflects ongoing bilateral discussions aimed at improving trade reciprocity and addressing national and economic security concerns.
The order directs multiple federal agencies to implement the suspension and affirms that it does not create enforceable legal rights for any party.
This EO declares a crime emergency in Washington, D.C., citing a dramatic rise in violent crime that threatens public safety and the effective functioning of the federal government.

The order invokes authority under the Home Rule Act to mandate that the Metropolitan Police Department provide services for federal purposes, including protecting federal property and maintaining law and order.
Operational control over these services is delegated to the Attorney General, who is tasked with monitoring the situation and advising the President on further actions.
The order emphasizes the urgency of restoring safety in the nation’s capital and asserts that current conditions are unacceptable, especially given D.C.’s status as the seat of federal governance.
This EO aims to democratize access to alternative assets for Americans participating in 401(k) and other defined-contribution retirement plans.

It addresses the disparity between public pension plans and individual retirement accounts in accessing high-performing, diversified investments such as private equity, real estate, digital assets, commodities, and infrastructure projects.

The EO directs the Department of Labor to reexamine and potentially revise its guidance under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1874 (“ERISA”) to reduce regulatory and litigation barriers that prevent fiduciaries from offering alternative asset options.

It also calls for collaboration with the SEC and other federal agencies to facilitate broader access to these investments, ensuring that fiduciaries can prudently enhance retirement outcomes for plan participants.
This EO aims to eliminate politicized and unlawful debanking practices by financial institutions and regulators.

It addresses concerns that individuals and businesses have been denied access to financial services based on political or religious beliefs or lawful business activities, citing past government-influenced surveillance and regulatory actions like "Operation Chokepoint." The EO mandates federal banking regulators to remove reputation-based risk assessments from guidance materials, identify and reinstate affected clients, and take disciplinary action against institutions found to have engaged in discriminatory debanking.
It also calls for a comprehensive strategy to prevent such practices and reinforces that banking decisions must be based on objective, risk-based criteria, not ideological bias.
This EO aims to overhaul federal grantmaking by enhancing oversight, accountability, and alignment with national interests.
It criticizes past grants for funding controversial or ineffective programs and mandates that agencies designate senior appointees to review funding announcements and discretionary awards.
The EO prohibits grants that promote racial preferences, deny biological sex, support illegal immigration, or undermine public safety and American values.
It calls for streamlined application processes, clearer benchmarks for success, and prioritization of institutions committed to reproducible, rigorous research.
Agencies must revise grant terms to allow termination for convenience and ensure discretionary funds are used effectively and transparently.

This EO imposes a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports from India due to its direct or indirect importation of Russian oil, which is deemed to perpetuate the national emergency declared in prior orders related to Russia’s actions in Ukraine.
The EO builds on EO 14066 and outlines exceptions, stacking rules with other tariffs, and procedures for monitoring and modifying the EO based on retaliation or compliance.

It delegates authority to various federal departments to enforce and adapt the EO and defines key terms like “Russian Federation oil” and “indirectly importing.” The EO emphasizes its legal consistency and severability, ensuring its provisions remain effective even if parts are invalidated.

**Establishing the White House Task Force on the 2028 Summer Olympics**(August 5, 2025)This EO establishes the White House Task Force on the 2028 Summer Olympics to coordinate federal efforts for hosting the Games.
Chaired by the president and Vice Chaired by the vice president, the Task Force includes key Cabinet members and senior White House officials.
It will oversee security, transportation, visa processing, and emergency preparedness, while promoting interagency collaboration and identifying regulatory barriers.

Housed within the Department of Homeland Security, the Task Force will operate until December 31, 2028, unless extended, and aims to ensure a safe, efficient, and globally welcoming Olympic experience.
This EO amends prior actions aimed at curbing the flow of illicit drugs, particularly fentanyl, across the U.S.-Canada border.
Citing Canada's insufficient cooperation and retaliatory trade measures, the EO raises tariffs on certain Canadian goods from 25 percent to 35 percent, effective August 1, 2025.
It also imposes a 40 percent tariff on Canadian products found to be transshipped to evade duties and mandates stricter enforcement by U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
The EO authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security to implement and monitor these measures, with provisions for further action if Canada fails to address the crisis or retaliates further.
It maintains exemptions under the USMCA and outlines updates to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to reflect these changes.
This EO modifies tariff rates to address ongoing concerns about large and persistent U.S. goods trade deficits, which have been deemed a national emergency under EO 14257.
It imposes new ad valorem duties on imports from certain foreign trading partners based on their level of reciprocity and alignment with U.S. economic and national security interests.
Countries that have made meaningful trade and security commitments will remain subject to adjusted tariffs until agreements are finalized.
The EO also introduces stricter penalties for transshipment intended to evade duties, including a 40 percent tariff and other sanctions.
It authorizes various federal agencies to implement and monitor these changes, with provisions for further action if foreign partners retaliate or fail to comply.
The Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (“HTSUS”) will be updated accordingly, and the EO maintains the validity of previous related executive actions.
This EO evokes previous directives and revitalizes the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, while reestablishing the Presidential Fitness Test.

Aimed at addressing the national health crisis—particularly among youth—the EO emphasizes the importance of physical activity, nutrition, and civic engagement in strengthening the nation’s vitality, economy, and military readiness.
The Council, composed of up to 30 presidential appointees, will advise on strategies to promote fitness, expand youth sports, and combat obesity and chronic disease.
The EO aligns with the upcoming 250th anniversary of the United States and major international sporting events, positioning health and fitness as central to national pride and resilience.
This EO suspending duty-free de minimis treatment for all countries, citing national emergencies related to illicit drug trafficking and persistent trade deficits.
The EO builds on previous actions targeting Canada, Mexico, China, and Hong Kong, and now applies globally to shipments not covered by specific exemptions.
It mandates that all non-postal shipments, regardless of value or origin, be subject to applicable duties and processed through formal customs entry.
Postal shipments will face new duty rates based on the country of origin’s tariff classification, with a transition period for carriers to adopt the new methodology.
The EO aims to close loopholes exploited by traffickers and ensure the effectiveness of tariffs imposed under earlier executive actions.
Implementation begins August 29, 2025.
This EO declares a national emergency in response to actions by the Government of Brazil that allegedly threaten U.S. national security, foreign policy, and economic interests.

The EO cites Brazilian officials, particularly Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, for engaging in censorship of U.S. persons, violating human rights, and politically persecuting former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro.
These actions include compelling U.S. tech companies to censor content, hand over user data, and face punitive measures for noncompliance.
As a response, the U.S. will impose an additional 40 percent ad valorem tariff on most Brazilian imports, with specific exemptions outlined in annexes.
The EO authorizes broad executive powers to enforce and adjust these measures, including potential escalation if Brazil retaliates, and mandates ongoing monitoring and reporting to Congress.
This EO aims to preserve and expand collegiate athletics, especially non-revenue and women's sports, amid growing threats from litigation and unregulated compensation practices.
It highlights the transformative role of college sports in education, leadership, and national success, including Olympic performance.
The EO criticizes the current system of third-party pay-for-play inducements and unrestricted athlete transfers, which it claims undermine fairness and sustainability.
It mandates increased scholarship opportunities based on athletic department revenues, prohibits improper third-party payments, and calls for federal agencies to develop enforcement plans.
It also seeks to clarify student-athlete status and protect college athletics from destabilizing lawsuits, while reinforcing the importance of college sports in developing U.S. Olympic talent.
This EO outlines a comprehensive federal strategy to address homelessness, public disorder, and drug addiction in urban areas.

It emphasizes restoring civil commitment for individuals with serious mental illness or substance use disorders who pose risks to themselves or others, and prioritizes enforcement against urban vagrancy, drug use, and squatting.

The EO directs federal agencies to redirect funding toward evidence-based treatment programs, increase accountability in homelessness assistance, and discourage “housing first” and “safe consumption” policies.
It also mandates stricter oversight of federal housing programs, including data sharing with law enforcement and protections for women and children.
The overarching goal is to restore public safety and order through institutional treatment and stricter enforcement mechanisms.
This EO establishes a national initiative to promote the global export of American full-stack artificial intelligence (“AI”) technologies.

It creates the American AI Exports Program, led by the Department of Commerce in coordination with other federal agencies, to support industry-led consortia in developing and deploying comprehensive AI packages—including hardware, software, data systems, and applications.
The EO aims to strengthen U.S. leadership in AI, reduce reliance on adversarial technologies, and mobilize federal financing tools to support selected export proposals.
It also outlines a unified federal strategy to promote American AI standards and foster international partnerships.
This EO is aimed at accelerating the federal permitting process for data center infrastructure critical to AI and national security.

The EO prioritizes the rapid development of large-scale AI data centers and related infrastructure by streamlining environmental reviews, leveraging federal lands, and offering financial incentives such as grants, loans, and tax breaks for qualifying projects.
It defines “Qualifying Projects” as those with significant capital investment, energy demands, or national security relevance.

The EO also revokes a previous AI infrastructure directive (EO 14141), promotes interagency coordination, and mandates expedited permitting processes under laws like the National Environmental Policy Act (“NEPA”) and FAST-41 to reduce regulatory delays and encourage private sector investment in AI-related technologies.
This EO is aimed at preventing what it describes as “woke” influences in artificial AI used by the federal government.
The EO criticizes diversity, equity, and inclusion (“DEI”) principles in AI, claiming they distort truth and accuracy by embedding ideological biases.
It mandates that federal agencies only procure large language models (“LLMs”) that adhere to two “Unbiased AI Principles”: truth-seeking and ideological neutrality.
The EO directs the OMB to issue implementation guidance within 120 days and requires agencies to ensure compliance in both new and existing contracts.
Exceptions are allowed for national security systems, and the EO emphasizes transparency without requiring disclosure of sensitive technical data.
This EO establishes a new "Schedule G" within the federal excepted service.
This schedule is designed for noncareer positions of policymaking or policy advocating nature that are typically subject to change with a presidential transition.
The EO fills a gap in existing schedules by creating a formal category for such roles, particularly to improve operations at the Department of Veterans Affairs.
It amends Civil Service Rule VI to include Schedule G and directs the Office of Personnel Management (“OPM”) to implement necessary regulations.
Appointments under Schedule G must align with the president’s policies but cannot consider political affiliation or activity.
This EO extends the suspension of additional ad valorem duties on certain foreign trading partners until August 1, 2025.
This extension follows previous orders aimed at addressing large and persistent U.S. goods trade deficits, which were deemed a threat to national security and the economy.
The suspension reflects the willingness of trading partners to address U.S. concerns, except for the People's Republic of China, which remains under separate tariff regulations.
The EO directs various government officials to implement necessary actions to effectuate these changes.
This EO aims to end subsidies for wind and solar energy, which are deemed unreliable and controlled by foreign adversaries.
The EO mandates the rapid elimination of "green" energy subsidies, strengthens the repeal of related tax credits, and ensures that taxpayer support for these energy sources is terminated.
The Department of the Treasury and the Department of the Interior are tasked with implementing these changes and reporting their progress within 45 days.
The goal is to enhance energy dominance, national security, economic growth, and fiscal health.
This EO establishes the "Make America Beautiful Again Commission" to prioritize the conservation of America's national parks and outdoor recreation areas.
The Commission, chaired by the Secretary of the Interior, aims to address issues like deferred maintenance and restricted access to public lands.
It will promote responsible stewardship, expand recreational access, and encourage voluntary conservation efforts.
The initiative seeks to balance economic growth with environmental preservation, ensuring future generations can enjoy America's natural beauty and outdoor heritage.
This EO aims to enhance America's national parks by increasing entry fees for foreign tourists while improving affordability for U.S. residents.

The Secretary of the Interior is tasked with developing strategies to boost revenue and enhance the recreational experience, including raising prices for nonresident passes and investing in park infrastructure.
The EO also emphasizes encouraging international tourism, reviewing maintenance backlogs, and ensuring that park management policies favor American residents.
Additionally, it revokes a previous memorandum on promoting diversity and inclusion in national parks.
This EO revokes several sanctions on Syria, recognizing positive changes under the new Syrian government led by President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
The EO terminates the national emergency declared in 2004 and removes various restrictions, including those related to property, export controls, and financial assistance.
However, it maintains accountability for human rights abuses and narcotics trafficking linked to the former regime of Bashar al-Assad.

The EO also directs the Secretary of State and other officials to take actions supporting a stable and peaceful Syria, while ensuring no relief is provided to terrorist organizations or human rights abusers.
This EO further extends the enforcement delay of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act concerning TikTok until September 17, 2025.
During this period, the Department of Justice is instructed not to enforce the Act or impose penalties for noncompliance.
The Attorney General is directed to issue guidance and letters to providers, ensuring no liability for actions taken during the specified periods.
The order emphasizes the exclusive authority of the Executive to enforce the Act, preventing states or private parties from attempting enforcement.
This EO implements the General Terms of the United States-United Kingdom Economic Prosperity Deal.
This historic trade agreement aims to enhance market access for American exports, particularly in agriculture, and reduce non-tariff barriers.
It establishes annual quotas for UK automotive imports at reduced tariff rates and commits both nations to strengthen supply chain security for steel and aluminum.
The deal also includes preferential treatment for UK pharmaceuticals and aims to bolster aerospace trade by eliminating tariffs on certain products.
Overall, the EO seeks to boost economic ties while addressing national security concerns.
This EO addresses the proposed acquisition of United States Steel Corporation by Nippon Steel Corporation.
Initially prohibited by President Biden due to national security concerns, the EO mandates a _de novo_ review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (“CFIUS”).
The review concluded that the acquisition could proceed if a national security agreement (“NSA”) is executed and adhered to by the parties involved.
The EO reserves the president's authority to issue further actions to protect national security and directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transmit the order to the relevant parties.
This EO aims to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of federal wildfire management.

It mandates the consolidation of wildland fire programs within the Departments of the Interior and Agriculture, encourages local preparedness through partnerships and technology, and promotes the use of innovative strategies like artificial intelligence (“AI”) and prescribed fires.
The EO also calls for the removal of regulatory barriers, the development of performance metrics, and the prioritization of excess military aircraft for wildfire mitigation.
Overall, the EO seeks to modernize and streamline wildfire prevention and response efforts across federal, state, and local levels.
This EO aims to reestablish the United States as a leader in supersonic flight by updating outdated regulations and embracing new technologies.
It directs the Federal Aviation Administration (“FAA”) to repeal prohibitions on overland supersonic flight and establish new noise-based certification standards.

The EO also mandates coordinated research and development efforts to advance supersonic technologies and promote international regulatory alignment, making supersonic flight safe, sustainable, and commercially viable.
This EO aims to restore American airspace sovereignty by addressing the threats posed by unmanned aircraft systems (“UAS”), or drones.

It establishes a Federal Task Force to develop solutions for UAS threats, mandates the FAA to create regulations for restricting drone flights over critical infrastructure, and enhances enforcement of laws against unlawful drone operations.
The EO also focuses on improving detection, tracking, and identification of drones, and building counter-UAS capacity to protect public safety, critical infrastructure, and national security.
**Unleashing American Drone Dominance**(June 6, 2025) This EO aims to accelerate the integration and commercialization of UAS in the United States.
It emphasizes the importance of drones in enhancing productivity, creating jobs, and modernizing aviation.

Key initiatives include enabling routine Beyond Visual Line of Sight (“BVLOS”) operations, deploying AI tools for regulatory processes, and establishing an Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (“eVTOL”) Pilot Program.
The EO also focuses on strengthening the domestic drone industry, securing supply chains, and promoting the export of American-made drones to global markets.
This EO aims to strengthen the nation's cybersecurity by amending previous orders.
It highlights the persistent cyber threats from foreign nations, particularly China, and outlines actions to improve digital infrastructure security.
Key amendments include establishing a consortium for secure software development, updating guidelines for patch deployment, preparing for post-quantum cryptography, and promoting AI in cyber defense.
The EO also aligns policies to reduce cyber risks and mandates labeling for consumer Internet-of-Things products.
This EO mandates the rapid development and deployment of advanced nuclear reactor technologies to enhance national security.
It emphasizes the need for resilient, secure, and reliable energy sources for critical defense facilities and Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) infrastructure.
The EO outlines policies to support private sector innovation, coordinate regulatory efforts, and utilize federal resources for uranium and plutonium.

It also includes directives for the Department of Defense and Department of Energy to establish programs for nuclear energy use at military installations and AI data centers, promote American nuclear exports, and ensure compliance with environmental regulations.
This EO aims to reform the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (“NRC”) to promote the development and deployment of nuclear energy in the United States.

It highlights the importance of nuclear energy for national and economic security and addresses the NRC's inefficiencies and overly cautious safety models that have hindered nuclear power development.
The EO mandates restructuring the NRC, revising its regulations, and adopting new technologies to expedite the licensing process.
The goal is to reestablish the United States as a global leader in nuclear energy, increase nuclear capacity, and create high-paying jobs while maintaining safety standards.
This EO aims to revitalize the development and deployment of advanced nuclear reactors in the United States.

It mandates the Department of Energy to expedite the review and approval process for new reactor designs, including microreactors and small modular reactors, to ensure they can be operational within two years of application submission.
The EO also establishes a pilot program for reactor construction outside of national laboratories and streamlines environmental reviews to facilitate faster deployment.
The goal is to enhance energy reliability, support various industries, and regain leadership in nuclear technology innovation.
This EO aims to revitalize the United States' nuclear energy sector to ensure national and economic security.
It outlines policies to increase nuclear fuel availability and production, secure supply chains, improve reactor licensing efficiency, and prepare the workforce for energy dominance.
The EO mandates the development of advanced fuel cycle capabilities, expansion of uranium conversion and enrichment, and prioritizes funding for nuclear plant construction and workforce training.
It emphasizes collaboration with domestic nuclear companies and federal agencies to enhance nuclear fuel management and recycling processes.
This EO aims to address the decline in public trust in science by ensuring transparency, rigor, and impartiality in scientific activities.
It mandates that agencies adopt "Gold Standard Science" practices, which include reproducibility, transparency, and unbiased peer review.
The EO also requires agencies to update their scientific integrity policies, make scientific data publicly available, and transparently communicate uncertainties.
This initiative seeks to rebuild confidence in government decisions informed by credible scientific evidence.
This EO modifies reciprocal tariff rates with the People's Republic of China.
This EO suspends the additional ad valorem duties imposed on Chinese imports for 90 days, reducing the rate from 34 percent to 10 percent.
The suspension reflects ongoing discussions with China to address trade imbalances and national security concerns.
The EO also includes adjustments to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States and mandates various departments to implement these changes.
The goal is to facilitate better trade relations and address the national emergency declared in previous orders.
This EO strives to implement the most-favored-nation pricing for prescription drugs.
The EO aims to address the disparity where Americans pay significantly higher prices for pharmaceuticals compared to other developed nations.

It mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to facilitate direct-to-consumer purchasing programs at the most-favored-nation price and to communicate price targets to pharmaceutical manufacturers.
If progress is not made, the EO outlines steps for rulemaking, importation of low-cost drugs, and enforcement actions against anti-competitive practices.
The goal is to ensure Americans receive the lowest possible prices for prescription drugs.
This EO establishes the National Center for Warrior Independence at the West Los Angeles VA Campus.
This initiative aims to provide comprehensive care, benefits, and services to homeless veterans, restoring their self-sufficiency and the warrior ethos.

The EO mandates the redirection of funds from services for illegal aliens to support the center, the use of vouchers for housing, and increased accountability within the Department of Veterans Affairs.
It also includes plans to reduce wait times for healthcare appointments and expand services at VA facilities, ensuring veterans receive the support they deserve.
This EO aims to increase efficiency at the Office of the Federal Register.
The EO aims to reduce publication delays and modernize computer systems to streamline the process of removing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations.
It mandates the Archivist of the United States to work with the Director of the Government Publishing Office to ensure fees for publication reflect actual costs and increased efficiencies.
The EO also requires reports on average publication times and fee schedules to be submitted to the OOMB.
This initiative supports the administration's deregulatory agenda and aims to reduce taxpayer costs.
This EO is aimed at reducing overcriminalization in federal regulations.
The EO highlights the excessive number of regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations, many of which carry criminal penalties, often without requiring a guilty mental state for conviction.

The EO seeks to ease the regulatory burden on Americans by disfavoring criminal enforcement of regulatory offenses, especially strict liability offenses, and promoting civil or administrative enforcement instead.
It mandates agencies to report and update lists of criminal regulatory offenses, ensure transparency in rulemaking, and consider mens rea standards for criminal offenses.
The EO excludes immigration and national security regulations from its scope.

This EO aims to promote domestic production of critical medicines by eliminating regulatory barriers that hinder the construction and expansion of pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities in the United States.

It directs the Food and Drug Administration, Environmental Protection Agency, and Army Corps of Engineers to streamline their review processes, eliminate duplicative requirements, and enhance coordination for environmental permits.

The EO also mandates improvements in the inspection of foreign manufacturing facilities and emphasizes the need for a resilient and affordable pharmaceutical supply chain to ensure national security and public health.

This EO aims to enhance the safety and security of biological research by halting federal funding for dangerous gain-of-function research conducted in countries with inadequate oversight, such as China.
It mandates the development of new guidelines to strengthen oversight, accountability, and transparency in federally funded life-science research.
The EO also calls for a strategy to manage risks associated with non-federally funded research and includes enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance.
The goal is to prevent catastrophic consequences while maintaining the United States' leadership in biotechnology and biosecurity.
This EO directs the cessation of federal funding for National Public Radio (“NPR”) and the Public Broadcasting Service (“PBS”) through the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (“CPB”).
It mandates the CPB Board to stop both direct and indirect funding to these entities, citing the need to ensure that taxpayer dollars do not support biased and partisan news coverage.
The EO also instructs all federal agencies to identify and terminate any funding to NPR and PBS, and to ensure compliance with non-discrimination statutes.
The goal is to uphold journalistic impartiality and prevent the use of public funds for media that do not meet these standards.
This EO establishes the Religious Liberty Commission to vigorously enforce protections for religious liberty enshrined in federal law.

The Commission, composed of diverse members appointed by the president, will produce a comprehensive report on the foundations and impact of religious liberty, identify emerging threats, and recommend strategies to preserve these freedoms.

It will advise the White House Faith Office and the Domestic Policy Council on religious liberty policies and partner with the Ambassador at Large for International Religious Freedom to promote religious liberty globally.
The Commission will terminate on July 4, 2026, unless extended by the president.
This EO streamlines the administration of tariffs on imported articles to prevent cumulative effects from overlapping tariffs.
It establishes procedures to determine which tariffs apply when an article is subject to multiple tariff actions, ensuring that the duty rates do not exceed what is necessary to achieve policy goals.
The EO applies to specific proclamations and EOs related to imports of automobiles, automobile parts, aluminum, steel, and duties addressing border issues.
It also directs relevant agencies to update guidance and enforcement mechanisms to reflect this policy.
This EO aims to empower state and local law enforcement to effectively combat crime and protect innocent citizens.
It establishes best practices for aggressive policing, enhances legal protections and resources for officers, and increases pay and benefits.
The EO also mandates the use of national security assets to support law enforcement and holds state and local officials accountable for obstructing criminal law enforcement.
Additionally, it prioritizes the legal defense of officers unjustly accused during their duties and seeks to end harmful equity policies that impede law enforcement activities.
This EO reinforces federal supremacy in immigration enforcement by identifying and penalizing "sanctuary" jurisdictions that obstruct federal immigration laws.
It mandates the publication of a list of such jurisdictions and imposes consequences, including the suspension or termination of federal funds.
The EO also directs the development of mechanisms to prevent federal benefits for aliens in these jurisdictions and ensures equal treatment of American citizens.
The goal is to restore the enforcement of U.S. immigration laws and protect national security.
This EO enhances promotes the safety and working conditions of America's truck drivers by enforcing English-language proficiency requirements for commercial motor vehicle operators.
It mandates the rescission of previous guidance that weakened these requirements and introduces new inspection procedures to ensure compliance.
The EO also calls for a review of non-domiciled commercial driver's licenses to identify irregularities and improve verification protocols.
Additionally, it directs the Secretary of Transportation to identify further actions to support truck drivers and ensure a secure and efficient motor carrier industry.
This EO aims to strengthen the United States' leadership in seabed mineral development to secure critical minerals essential for national security and economic prosperity.
It outlines policies to expedite domestic capabilities for exploring, characterizing, collecting, and processing seabed mineral resources while maintaining environmental standards.

The EO emphasizes enhancing coordination among federal agencies, supporting investment in deep-sea science and technology, and establishing international partnerships to counter foreign influence, particularly from China.
It also seeks to create a robust domestic supply chain for critical minerals to support economic growth, reindustrialization, and military preparedness.

**Strengthening Probationary Periods in the Federal Service**(April 24, 2025)This EO aims to strengthen the probationary and trial periods for federal employees to ensure a high-quality and efficient workforce.
It mandates that agencies must affirmatively determine the suitability of employees before finalizing their appointments.

The EO repeals existing regulations that limit agency actions during these periods and introduces new rules requiring agency certification that an employee's continued employment is in the public interest.
The goal is to prevent underperforming employees from gaining tenure and to enhance the overall effectiveness of the federal service.

This EO promotes AI education by establishing a task force to coordinate federal efforts, creating public-private partnerships for K–12 AI literacy, and enhancing AI training for educators and workforce development programs.
It aims to ensure Americans are equipped with AI skills from early education through lifelong learning.

This EO aims to eliminate disparate-impact liability to uphold meritocracy and equality of opportunity, revoking previous regulations and directing agencies to deprioritize enforcement of statutes that include such liability.
It mandates a review and amendment of existing regulations to ensure compliance with constitutional principles and civil rights laws.
This EO reinstates common sense school discipline policies by rejecting discriminatory equity ideologies and emphasizing discipline based on student behavior.
It mandates new guidance and coordination among federal and state agencies to ensure non-discriminatory practices in school discipline.
This EO aims to enhance workforce development by consolidating federal programs, expanding registered apprenticeships, and improving transparency and accountability.
It focuses on aligning investments with reindustrialization needs and equipping American workers with skills for high-demand jobs.
This EO establishes the White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges and Universities (“HBCUs”) to enhance their capacity for providing high-quality education and economic opportunities.
It aims to foster public-private partnerships, improve infrastructure, and promote student success and retention at HBCUs.
This EO reforms higher education accreditation to ensure institutions provide high-quality, valuable education without unlawful discrimination.
It mandates accountability for accreditors, promotes intellectual diversity, and aims to reduce unnecessary costs and barriers for institutions.
This EO mandates robust enforcement of foreign funding disclosure requirements for higher education institutions to protect American interests.
It directs the Secretary of Education to ensure transparency, reverse previous administration's actions that allowed secrecy, and hold institutions accountable for non-compliance.
This EO aims to restore American seafood competitiveness by reducing regulatory burdens, combating unfair trade practices, and promoting ethical sourcing.
It directs the Secretary of Commerce to revise or rescind overly burdensome regulations and develop strategies to enhance domestic seafood production and market access.
This EO mandates federal agencies to prioritize commercially available products and services in procurement to reduce unnecessary spending and integrate private sector innovations.
It requires a thorough review of non-commercial procurements and regular reporting to ensure compliance and cost-effectiveness.
This EO revokes previous orders that mandated federal facilities to be located in central business districts and historic properties, allowing agencies to choose cost-effective locations.
It directs the General Services Administration to amend regulations to align federal office space management with this new policy.
This EO mandates an investigation into the national security risks posed by the U.S. reliance on imported processed critical minerals and their derivative products.
It aims to identify vulnerabilities, assess the impact of foreign competition, and recommend measures to ensure a resilient and secure supply chain for these essential materials.
This EO aims to lower prescription drug prices by enhancing transparency, promoting competition, and reforming Medicare and Medicaid payment models.
It includes measures to streamline drug importation, stabilize Medicare Part D premiums, and ensure affordable access to life-saving medications for low-income individuals.

This EO aims to streamline federal procurement by reforming the Federal Acquisition Regulation (“FAR”) to remove unnecessary regulations, enhance efficiency, and ensure alignment with policy objectives.
It mandates a comprehensive review and amendment of the FAR to support simplicity, usability, and economic or national security interests.

This EO modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to increase tariffs on imports from China in response to their retaliatory tariffs, while temporarily suspending specific tariffs for other trading partners who have shown willingness to address trade imbalances.
It aims to protect U.S. national and economic security by addressing trade deficits and unfair trade practices.

This EO addresses risks associated with Susman Godfrey LLP by suspending security clearances, terminating contracts, and limiting access to federal resources due to their discriminatory practices and activities undermining American interests.
It mandates reviews and actions to ensure alignment with national security and federal policies.

This EO aims to modernize defense acquisitions by accelerating procurement processes, revitalizing the defense industrial base, and incentivizing innovation and risk-taking within the acquisition workforce.
It mandates comprehensive reviews and reforms to streamline operations and enhance the efficiency of defense procurement.
This EO establishes policies to enhance the competitiveness and capabilities of the U.S. maritime industry.
The EO aims to ensure national security and economic prosperity through a strong maritime sector.
This EO orders the repeal of regulations deemed unlawful or unnecessary to reduce regulatory burdens and promote economic growth.
The EO directs agencies to review and repeal such regulations.
This EO directs federal agencies to identify and eliminate anti-competitive regulatory barriers that hinder economic growth and innovation.
The EO aims to promote a competitive economic environment.
This EO implements a zero-based regulatory budgeting approach to eliminate unnecessary regulations and promote domestic energy production.
The EO directs federal agencies to identify and eliminate anti-competitive regulatory barriers.
This EO enhances accountability and transparency in the foreign defense sales system.
The EO aims to strengthen the security capabilities of allies, invigorate the U.S. defense industrial base, and improve financing options for partners.
It directs the Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense to implement policies to streamline foreign defense sales.
This EO orders the repeal of the 13,000-word regulation defining “showerhead” to restore a straightforward definition and ensure adequate water pressure.
The Secretary of Energy is directed to publish a notice rescinding the regulation, effective 30 days from publication.
This EO modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to increase duties on imports from China in response to retaliatory tariffs imposed by the PRC.
The amendment aims to address the threat to national security and the economy by increasing tariffs on low-value imports.
This EO designates coal as a “mineral” under EO 14241, removing regulatory barriers to coal production.
The EO encourages the utilization of coal to meet growing domestic energy demands and supports coal exports.
It also directs relevant agencies to identify coal resources on federal lands and lift barriers to coal mining.
This EO exempts certain coal-fired power plants from compliance with stringent emissions standards for two years beyond the rule’s compliance date.
The exemption aims to ensure the reliability of the nation’s power supply and support the coal sector by addressing the technological infeasibility of current emissions-control standards.
This EO directs the Attorney General to identify and take action against state laws and policies that burden the use of domestic energy resources and are unconstitutional or unenforceable.

The EO targets state laws addressing climate change, environmental justice, and carbon emissions, prioritizing actions against those that impose significant barriers to interstate and international trade.
This EO orders the Secretary of Energy to streamline processes for issuing emergency orders under the Federal Power Act during periods of anticipated interruptions.
The secretary must develop a uniform methodology for analyzing reserve margins and identify regions with unacceptable reserve margins.
The EO aims to safeguard the reliability and security of the electric grid during periods of high demand.
This EO directs the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (“CFIUS”) to conduct a _de novo_ review of the acquisition of U.S. Steel by Nippon Steel Corporation.
The review will assess national security risks and provide recommendations within 45 days on whether proposed measures are sufficient to mitigate identified risks.
The memorandum emphasizes confidentiality and adherence to national security review procedures.
This EO extends the enforcement delay specified in EO 14166 until June 19, 2025.

During this period, the Department of Justice shall take no action to enforce the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act or impose any penalties against entities for noncompliance, including for distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary-controlled applications.
The Attorney General is directed to issue written guidance and letters to providers stating there has been no violation of the statute and no liability for conduct during the specified period.
This EO further amends duties to address the synthetic opioid supply chain from China, specifically targeting low-value imports.
It removes duty-free treatment for certain low-value goods from China and Hong Kong to close loopholes that allow illicit substances to enter the United States.
This measure is part of broader efforts to combat the synthetic opioid crisis.
This EO introduces reciprocal tariffs to address trade practices that contribute to large U.S. trade deficits.
It aims to create a fairer trading environment by imposing tariffs that match those of U.S. trading partners, thereby protecting domestic industries and national security.
This EO addresses issues in the live entertainment industry, such as ticket scalping and excessive fees by middlemen.

It directs the Federal Trade Commission ("FTC") and the Attorney General to enforce competition laws, ensure price transparency, and prevent unfair, deceptive, and anti-competitive conduct in the secondary ticketing market.
This EO establishes the United States Investment Accelerator within the Department of Commerce to facilitate and accelerate investments above $1 billion in the United States.

The Investment Accelerator will assist investors in navigating regulatory processes, reduce regulatory burdens, increase access to national resources, and work with state governments to increase both domestic and foreign investments.
This EO directs efforts to enhance the safety and aesthetics of the District of Columbia.
It mandates improvements in public infrastructure, increased law enforcement presence, and initiatives to beautify public spaces.
The EO aims to create a safer and more attractive environment for residents and visitors.
This EO mandates the revision of educational materials to ensure accurate representation of American history.
It aims to eliminate biased narratives and promote a balanced understanding of historical events.
The EO directs the Department of Education to collaborate with historians and educators to develop curricula that reflect the true history of the United States.

This EO excludes certain agencies and agency subdivisions from federal labor-management relations programs due to their primary functions in intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work.

The EO amends previous exclusions and adds new ones, including various departments and subdivisions within the Department of State, Department of Defense, Department of Treasury, Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Justice, Department of Health and Human Services, and Department of Homeland Security.
These exclusions are intended to enhance national security by ensuring that labor-management relations do not compromise the critical functions of these agencies.
This proclamation imposes a 25 percent tariff on imports of automobiles and certain automobile parts to address national security concerns.
The Secretary of Commerce's investigation found that these imports threaten to impair the national security of the United States.
The tariffs aim to protect the domestic automotive industry from unfair competition and ensure a resilient industrial base.
This EO addresses the detrimental conduct of Jenner & Block LLP, including partisan representations and discriminatory practices.
The order mandates the suspension of security clearances for individuals at Jenner & Block and reviews their access to Government resources.
These measures are intended to mitigate risks associated with the firm's actions and ensure compliance with the administration’s ethical standards.
This EO enforces federal election requirements to ensure that votes are cast and received by Election Day, prohibits non-citizens from voting, and mandates voter identification.
The EO aims to maintain free, fair, and honest elections by addressing issues such as mail-in voting and ballot counting.
It seeks to uphold the integrity of the electoral process and prevent potential abuses.
This EO aims to promote financial integrity and operational efficiency by enforcing controls and ensuring accountability for transactions flowing through the United States General Fund.
The EO addresses the fragmentation of disbursing authority and the need for accurate financial information to safeguard taxpayer dollars.
It mandates measures to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse in government financial operations.

This memorandum directs the immediate declassification of materials related to the FBI’s Crossfire Hurricane investigation, with exceptions for those proposed for redaction by the FBI and those protected by law.
The Attorney General is instructed to make the declassified materials available to the public without delay.
This action is taken to promote transparency and accountability in the investigation process.
This EO mandates the transition to electronic payments for all federal disbursements and receipts by September 30, 2025.
The EO aims to reduce costs, enhance security, and defend against financial fraud by phasing out paper checks and promoting digital payment methods.
This modernization effort is intended to streamline financial transactions and improve the efficiency of government operations.
This EO imposes a 25 percent tariff on goods imported from countries that continue to import Venezuelan oil.
The EO is issued in response to the national emergency posed by Venezuela's destabilizing actions, including support for transnational criminal organizations like the Tren de Aragua gang.
The tariffs aim to sever financial lifelines of the Maduro regime and curb its influence, thereby addressing the threats to U.S. national security.
This memorandum addresses unethical conduct by lawyers and law firms that pose threats to national security, public safety, or election integrity.
It highlights specific examples of misconduct, such as fraudulent asylum claims and unethical litigation practices, which undermine the legal system.
The memorandum mandates accountability and enforcement of regulations governing attorney conduct to prevent such abuses and protect the integrity of the legal system.
This memorandum directs the immediate revocation of security clearances and access to classified information for specified individuals, including Antony Blinken, Jacob Sullivan, and others.
It mandates that executive departments and agencies take all necessary actions to revoke these clearances and access, ensuring that these individuals no longer have access to sensitive information.
This action is taken to safeguard national security and prevent potential risks associated with unauthorized access.
This EO revokes EO 14237, which previously addressed risks associated with Paul Weiss.
The firm has acknowledged the wrongdoing of its former partner and agreed to implement policy changes that promote equality, justice, and merit-based hiring.
Paul Weiss commits to providing $40 million in pro bono services aimed at supporting veterans, ensuring fairness in the justice system, and combating anti-Semitism.
**Stopping Waste, Fraud, and Abuse by Eliminating Information Silos**(March 20, 2025): This EO addresses inefficiencies caused by information silos within federal agencies.
It mandates improved data sharing and coordination to prevent waste, fraud, and abuse.

The EO requires agencies to identify and eliminate barriers to information sharing, establish protocols for inter-agency data exchange, and implement technologies that facilitate seamless communication.
By breaking down these silos, the administration aims to enhance overall government efficiency, improve decision-making, and ensure that resources are used more effectively.

**Strengthening the Suitability and Fitness of the Federal Workforce**(March 20, 2025): This memorandum delegates authority to the Office of Personnel Management (“OPM”) to make final suitability determinations and take actions regarding federal employees based on post-appointment conduct.
The OPM is tasked with proposing regulations to amend existing rules, ensuring that employees meet high standards of fitness and suitability.
The memorandum also requires agencies to refer cases of post-appointment misconduct to the OPM for final determination.
This initiative aims to maintain a high standard of integrity and performance within the federal workforce.

**Eliminating Waste and Saving Taxpayer Dollars by Consolidating Procurement** (March 20, 2025): This EO consolidates federal procurement for common goods and services within the General Services Administration (“GSA”).
The EO mandates that all executive departments and agencies submit proposals to the GSA for conducting procurement activities.
The GSA is then responsible for creating a comprehensive plan to centralize procurement, eliminating duplication and inefficiencies.
This consolidation is expected to save taxpayer dollars, streamline procurement processes, and improve the quality of goods and services acquired by the government.
**Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production**(March 20, 2025): This EO aims to boost domestic mineral production to enhance national security and reduce reliance on foreign sources.
It calls for expedited permitting processes and prioritizes mineral production activities on federal lands.
The order defines "mineral" broadly to include critical minerals, uranium, copper, potash, gold, and other elements.
Agencies involved in mineral production permitting are required to identify and expedite priority projects.
The order also encourages the use of the Defense Production Act to expand domestic mineral production capacity.

**Improving Education Outcomes by Empowering Parents, States, and Communities**(March 20, 2025): This EO seeks to close the Department of Education and return authority over education to states and local communities.
The EO argues that federal control has failed to improve educational outcomes, citing low proficiency rates in reading and math among students.
It mandates the Secretary of Education to take steps to facilitate the closure of the department while ensuring the uninterrupted delivery of services.
The goal is to empower local entities to make decisions that best serve their students and families.

**Removing Discrimination and Discriminatory Equity Ideology from the Foreign Service**(March 19, 2025): This memorandum directs the removal of policies promoting discriminatory equity ideology from the Foreign Service.
It mandates merit-based hiring and promotion, aiming to eliminate unconstitutional discrimination based on race or other protected characteristics.
The Secretary of State is instructed to revise the criteria for tenure and promotion to remove references to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility.
The memorandum also requires an investigation into any current Foreign Service members who may have engaged in discriminatory practices.
**Achieving Efficiency Through State and Local Preparedness** (March 19, 2025): This EO emphasizes the importance of state and local governments in national resilience and preparedness.
It calls for updating federal policies to empower local decision-making and investments in infrastructure.
The EO mandates the creation of a National Resilience Strategy and a review of critical infrastructure policies to enhance security and reduce taxpayer burdens.
By empowering state and local governments, the administration aims to improve overall preparedness and response to emergencies.

**Invocation of the Alien Enemies Act Regarding the Invasion of the United States by Tren De Aragua**(March 15, 2025): This proclamation invokes the Alien Enemies Act to address the threat posed by Tren de Aragua, a Venezuelan criminal organization.
The act authorizes measures to combat their illegal activities, including drug trafficking and irregular warfare.
The proclamation highlights the group's infiltration into the United States and its collaboration with other criminal organizations.
The goal is to protect national security by taking decisive action against these threats.

**Addressing Risks from Paul Weiss**(March 14, 2025): This EO suspends security clearances for individuals associated with Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP and prohibits government contracts with the firm.
The EO cites unethical practices and discrimination within the firm, including actions that undermine American principles and safety.
Specific incidents involving the firm, such as hiring unethical attorneys and engaging in discriminatory practices, are highlighted as reasons for these measures.

**Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy**(March 14, 2025): This EO eliminates non-statutory functions and reduces statutory functions of several governmental entities deemed unnecessary.
The affected entities include the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, United States Agency for Global Media, and others.
The EO requires these entities to report on their compliance and justify any remaining statutory functions.
The goal is to streamline government operations, reduce waste, and enhance accountability.
This memorandum directs federal agencies to enforce Rule 65(c), which requires parties seeking preliminary injunctions against the federal government to provide financial security.
This ensures that the government is compensated for costs and damages if the injunction is later found to be wrongly issued.

The memorandum addresses the issue of activist organizations obtaining sweeping injunctions that undermine the democratic process and directs agencies to request that federal courts require plaintiffs to post security to cover potential costs and damages.
This EO aims to revise the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (“PSLF”) Program to exclude organizations engaged in activities deemed illegal or harmful to national security.
The Secretary of Education, in coordination with the Secretary of the Treasury, is tasked with proposing these revisions.

The order highlights the misuse of the PSLF Program by the prior administration and seeks to ensure that taxpayer funds are not used to subsidize illegal activities, including illegal immigration, human smuggling, child trafficking, and other harmful actions.
This EO establishes a task force to coordinate the United States' preparations for hosting the FIFA World Cup 2026, which will be the largest sporting event in history.
The task force, chaired by the president and vice-chaired by the vice president, includes key members from various executive departments and agencies.
The task force will assist in planning, organizing, and executing events surrounding the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup and the 2026 FIFA World Cup, promoting economic growth and tourism through sport.
This EO establishes a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a United States Digital Asset Stockpile to manage the nation's digital asset holdings.
It aims to harness the strategic value of Bitcoin and other digital assets for national prosperity and security.
By creating these reserves, the administration seeks to position the United States as a leader in the digital economy and ensure the stability and security of its digital asset infrastructure.
This EO amends previous duties imposed on Mexican goods to address the flow of illicit drugs across the southern border.
It adjusts tariffs on certain automotive parts and potash to minimize disruption to the U.S. automotive industry while maintaining efforts to combat drug trafficking.
Specifically, the order exempts certain automotive parts from additional tariffs and reduces the additional rate of duty on potash from 25 percent to 10 percent.
These modifications aim to balance economic interests with the need to enhance border security and reduce the smuggling of illicit substances.
This EO addresses the risks posed by the law firm Perkins Coie LLP, citing its involvement in undermining democratic elections and engaging in discriminatory practices.
It calls for the suspension of security clearances held by individuals at Perkins Coie and the cessation of government services provided to the firm.
This EO amends previous duties imposed on Canadian goods to address the flow of illicit drugs across the northern border.
It adjusts tariffs on certain automotive parts and potash to minimize disruption to the U.S. automotive industry while maintaining efforts to combat drug trafficking.
This EO renames the Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge in Texas to the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge in memory of Jocelyn Nungaray, a 12-year-old girl tragically murdered by illegal aliens.
The renaming aims to honor her life and passion for animals while highlighting the consequences of previous immigration policies.
The order serves as a tribute to Jocelyn's memory and a reminder of the importance of effective immigration enforcement.
This EO increases tariffs on products from China to 20 percent in response to the continued influx of synthetic opioids, including fentanyl, from China.
